consistency and voice: repeated phrases, tonal drift, name collisions, redundant sections, flavor-vs-rules balance

payload.name: hol-rulebook
payload.problem_domain: Heroes of Legend TTRPG rulebook chapter review and disposition

payload.statement:
Chapter under review: ch15 (quarto-book/chapters/15-equipment.qmd), "Equipment", 240 lines.

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan.
Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files a finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope

Findings cite [file:line] in the chapter (15-equipment.qmd). Mechanics
findings state the broken value and the expected value. Cross-chapter checks
use the authoritative chapters as the reference, not this chapter (core
rules = ch06, conditions table = ch13, combat maneuvers/cover = ch13,
damage budget = ch08, skills roster = ch07, armor = ch16, starting kits =
ch02/ch05, GM rules = ch19, reference tables = ch22).

Disposition classes (for the librarian's synthesis):
  mechanical    - safe to implement as a micro-PR (headings, tables, wording,
                  em-dashes, single-cell refs, budget rows)
  substantive   - needs a dispatched implementation pass (multi-file, new content)
  design-decision - needs Bruce's ruling; implement the recommended default,
                  flagged veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md

Standing book conventions are in force: zero em-dashes in book text; damage
budgets flat at Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21; card costs 2/4/8;
Adept prereqs exactly 2, Master exactly 3; no flat +N damage riders anywhere
in the book (a damage bonus must be a budget row, a Basic-card floor of
1/2/3 + attribute, or a "+1 damage tier" bump); recurring damage must use
the leveled condition vocabulary (Burning X, Frozen X, Poisoned X) with the
condition number scaling magnitude, not bespoke "ongoing" phrasing.
Violations of these conventions are findings, not questions.

payload.argument: Refute: the chapter must change; a mechanics audit names thirteen defects, several of them flat rider law or one-roll violations. (1) [15-equipment:195] The Charge table's Strong cell reads 'Strong + 3', a flat +3 damage rider. The book's legal bonus forms are a budget row, the Basic unarmed floor with an attribute, or a one-tier bump, so the expected value is 'Strong' capped with no rider. Class: mechanical, single-cell edit. (2) [15-equipment:239] The vehicle chase is unresolvable: it prescribes 1d6 per round with no success threshold, the Speed column holds text ('Draft animal', 'Oars or sail', 'Sail') so 'higher Speed rating' cannot be evaluated, and equal success counts have no tie-break. Expected: a 3d6 one-roll opposed contest with a defined success criterion per ch06. Class: substantive, needs a dispatch. (3) [15-equipment:132, 148] Oil and Volatile Reagents impose recurring fire harm that persists until the victim expends an action to extinguish it; expected vocabulary is the leveled condition Burning 1 from the ch13 conditions table (takes X damage per round, spend an action to end). Class: mechanical. (4) [15-equipment:147] The torch deals flat '1 fire damage on hit' as an improvised weapon, off the in-chapter improvised curve; expected 1/1/2 fire damage like crowbar and hammer. Class: mechanical. (5) [15-equipment:120, 125] Improvised weapon parentheticals '1/1/2 damage' drop the attribute floor; the Basic Unarmed card is 1/1/2 + Brawn (ch09:287-291), so expected is '(1/1/2 + Brawn)' or a pointer to that card. Class: mechanical. (6) [15-equipment:52] 'Missile and thrown attacks add Agility' contradicts the budget chapter, which states arrows, missile ammunition, and thrown weapons are flat with no attribute added (08-disciplines:193, 195), and the Basic Archery/Thrown cards are flat 1/2/3 (09-talents-abilities:259-277). Expected: missile and thrown attacks are flat, no attribute. Class: mechanical. (7) [15-equipment:25-43, 52 vs 08-disciplines:197] The budget chapter defers the weapon damage curve (dagger 1/2/3 up to greatsword 3/5/8) to this chapter, but the weapon table has no damage column and line 52 claims the weapon never changes damage. Expected: add a Weak/Standard/Strong column, or coordinate a fix of the ch08 deferral. Recommended default: keep the cards-are-damage design (ch09:239 states weapon disciplines gate stronger cards, not higher damage) and correct ch08's deferral; this also explains why the Crossbow (1 Archery, Loading) is strictly worse than the Longbow (1 Archery) with no way to differentiate. Class: design-decision, needs Bruce. (8) [15-equipment:199 vs 13-combat:60] This chapter redefines Command as mount direction with Survival/Nature control checks, while ch13 defines Command as the mount taking an extra move; expected alignment is that movement is free and Command grants the extra move, with control checks stated as a separate rule. Class: substantive, cross-chapter reconciliation. (9) [15-equipment:201, 207] Odd flat modifiers (-1/+1 and a '-2 reduced to -1' half-step at Adept) sit outside the book's even-step difficulty ladder (+4/+2/0/-2/-4/-6) and Boon/Bane convention; expected is Bane/Boon phrasing or even steps. Recommended default: convert the moving-mount penalty to Bane, ignored at Adept+ Survival/Nature. Class: design-decision. (10) [15-equipment:116, 126] Rest vocabulary is stale: 'full rest' should be 'long rest' per ch19, and 'recover half HP (rounded down) from rest' is ambiguous against ch19's level-based recovery; expected is 'half the long-rest recovery, rounded down'. Class: mechanical. (11) [15-equipment:118] Caltrops halving the victim's Speed for the following round is bespoke; expected is the Slowed X condition with a fixed feet reduction (13-combat:187). Class: mechanical. (12) [15-equipment:25-43] The weapons Cost column is blank for every entry except Throwing Dagger at 2 gp; expected is populated prices or a removed column. Class: mechanical. (13) [15-equipment:222-223] 'Draft animal (-2)' in the vehicle Speed column is undefined notation; expected is a defined feet value or an explicit rule. Class: mechanical. Verified clean: crowbar Boon and draft-horse Bane match ch06; Tower Shield 'half cover' matches ch13's cover table; weapon Discipline combos match the sanctioned prereq shapes (08-disciplines:162-164); armor values match ch16; 'Standard 9-14'/'Strong 15+' tier notation matches ch06 examples.

evidence.claim: The chase rule calls for a 1d6 roll each round with no success threshold and no numeric Speed rating to compare, so it cannot be resolved.
The mounted charge upgrades a Strong result to 'Strong + 3', a flat damage rider the book forbids.
Oil and Volatile Reagents impose bespoke recurring fire damage that must instead use the Burning condition vocabulary.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: 1 ongoing fire damage until they spend an action

evidence.claim: The authoritative budget chapter promises a per-weapon damage curve living in the Equipment chapter, which this chapter never supplies.
The conditions table defines recurring damage through the leveled Burning X condition ending when an action is spent.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Burning X | Takes X damage per round

payload.argument: The chapter fails an empirical audit on five counts, each verified against the authoritative chapters. (1) The mount-charge table's top cell [15-equipment:195] grants a flat point bonus on a Strong result, which violates the book-wide law that damage bonuses are budget rows, Basic-card floors, or one-tier bumps; the same fact is stated a different way in the Charge weapon-maneuver card [09-talents-abilities:447-455] as a one-tier shift with no extra points, so the dual implementations disagree and the top cell should read a tier cap with no flat adder. (2) Two gear rows [15-equipment:132, 148] impose a bespoke recurring-fire phrase; the mechanics match Burning 1 exactly [13-combat:171] [21-glossary:129], so the rows should invoke the leveled condition instead of the nonstandard wording. (3) The improvised-weapon parentheticals [15-equipment:120, 125] use a 1/1/2 curve that appears nowhere in the weapon ladder [08-disciplines:197], which runs 1/2/3 to 3/5/8; the only 1/1/2 in the book is the Basic Unarmed card [09-talents-abilities:287-295], so these rows are off-curve and should be set to the 1/2/3 floor or given an explicit improvised rule. (4) The vehicle chase contest [15-equipment:239] never defines what a single roll counts as a success, so the win condition (3 successes) is unimplementable; it also compares Speed ratings that live in different units for the two sides it advertises, since the wagon's Speed is its draft animal's rating [15-equipment:174, 221, 231] while the chasing horse's is its own 60 ft [15-equipment:170], which is a 10-point gap the single +1 rule cannot represent. (5) The weapons table [15-equipment:25-43] lists every cost cell as empty, but the same table's Throwing Dagger row shows a gp price and the rest of the chapter is built around gp pricing, so 16 of 17 weapon rows are missing values. Stance is refute; fixes 1, 2, and 5 are mechanical micro-PRs, fix 3 is a design-decision with a recommended default of the 1/2/3 floor, and fix 4 needs a definition of a success plus a Speed-comparison rule. Supporting checks that held: the @sec-chapter-talents-abilities anchor resolves [09-talents-abilities:1], all four cross-references resolve, the {#sec-chapter-equipment} anchor is referenced by ch08 and ch02 and resolves, half cover exists in the Cover table [13-combat:332], Command is a basic maneuver [13-combat:60], the named skills Survival and Nature are on the roster [07-skills:111, 128], Boon and Bane are defined [21-glossary:27, 29], the starting-kit 10 gp fund matches ch02 and ch05, and the charge table's first two rows agree with the tier-shift wording elsewhere.

evidence.claim: The charge table's Strong row adds a flat point bonus to the result, contradicting the book-wide rule that damage bonuses are tier bumps, not point riders; the same fact is stated as a one-tier shift in the Charge maneuver card [09-talents-abilities:447-455].

The conditions table already contains a leveled fire condition whose effect (one fire damage per round, ended by an action) is exactly what the oil and alchemist's-fire rows describe, so the equipment rows should invoke the condition rather than bespoke recurring-fire wording.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Burning X | Takes X damage per round

evidence.claim: The authoritative weapon damage curve runs from a 1/2/3 floor to a 3/5/8 ceiling, so the improvised-weapon parentheticals' 1/1/2 matches no row in the ladder and is off-curve.

Enumerating the chase contest: a success is never defined, so the 3-success win condition is unimplementable; and a wagon's Speed is its draft animal's rating (40 ft) while a chasing horse's is 60 ft, a 10-point gap the single +1 rule cannot represent, so wagon-versus-horse is unwinnable for the wagon.

The weapons table shows a gp price only in the Throwing Dagger row; the other 16 weapon rows have empty cost cells despite the chapter's gp pricing convention, so the table is incomplete as a publishable unit.
The @sec-chapter-talents-abilities cross-reference target anchor exists at the top of the Talents chapter, so the chapter's two references to it resolve.
The Cover table contains a half-cover row, so the tower shield's half-cover claim is not a phantom and resolves against the authoritative cover rules.

The chapter's own Charge table's first two rows (Weak to Standard, Standard to Strong) agree with the one-tier-shift wording used by the Charge maneuver card, so only the top Strong cell is the outlier.

payload.argument: The chapter's mechanical architecture splits on a single fork: the two charge rules (the land Charge maneuver in the talents chapter and the mounted Charge Attack table here) are treated as independent mechanics, and the mounted table expresses its top result as a flat additive number, a category the book's damage law forbids everywhere else. I stress-tested the charge table, the chase contest, the consumable fire wording, the improvised-weapon parenthetical, the mount economy, the crossbow, and the crowbar Boon line. Counter-examples: (1) Charge stacking, the fork: the mounted table [15-equipment:195] maps Strong to "Strong + 3"; a rider with the land Charge maneuver [09-talents-abilities:447] already attacks at +1 tier and can also move 20 ft straight on a mount, so both fire; a greatsword (3/5/8 plus Brawn +2) lands Strong for 10, the mount table adds a flat 3 (13), and a book tier bump (Battle Cry [05-classes:503], Read the Room [05-classes:502]) stacks on top. Broken value: 13+ from one hit where the Adept budget rows cap at 12; expected: one charge benefit per attack, no flat addition. Disposition: mechanical. (2) Flat rider breaks the book's damage law: "Strong + 3" is a flat +N damage rider; the book allows damage only as budget rows, Basic-card 1/2/3 + attribute floors, or +1 damage-tier bumps. Broken value: flat +3 on a damage value; expected: a tier expression or a rider effect (free attack, knock Prone) instead of a number. Disposition: mechanical. (3) No "once per attack" clause: two-weapon fighting's off-hand attack after a mounted charge can also claim the +3, and nothing limits the flat bonus to the charge attack itself. Expected: the bonus applies to exactly one attack per charge. Disposition: mechanical. (4) Chase stall: both sides roll a d6, the higher-Speed side gains +1, first to 3 successes wins, ties are complications that never advance the score [15-equipment:239]. A draft-animal wagon vs a riding horse gives the horse +1 per round; the wagon wins a round only about 28% of the time, and a player who never rolls above the pursuer stalls forever, since ties produce narration, not progress. No bound on rounds, no rule for equal Speed. Expected: chases terminate in a bounded number of rounds, ties resolving toward the faster side or escalating a clock. Disposition: substantive. (5) Vehicle Speed is undefined for the contest: the table lists Speed as "Draft animal" [15-equipment:220] and "Draft animal (-2)" [15-equipment:222] with no number, so the higher-Speed comparison has no defined value for the flagship wagon case. Broken value: undefined Speed in a rule that compares Speed; expected: a concrete value or explicit pointer. Disposition: mechanical. (6) Improvised weapon never defined here: Crowbar and Hammer carry a (1/1/2 damage) parenthetical [15-equipment:120,125], the torch deals 1 fire damage on hit [15-equipment:147], oil deals 2 on hit [15-equipment:132], yet the chapter references an improvised-weapon rule without defining it; the only definition in the book is the Odd class ability [05-classes:590], a flat Standard 4 once per scene, a different number. Broken value: three incompatible improvised damage definitions; expected: one rule stated here that the consumables reference. Disposition: mechanical. (7) Oil as budget breaker: at 1 sp a flask, a player throws oil every round for 2 fire damage plus a recurring burn that costs the target an action to end [15-equipment:132]. No once-per-scene, no save, no DR clause, no carry limit; at level 1 this out-damages every Basic attack card for trivial coin. Expected: a per-encounter limit, a capped stack, or a value consistent with the Basic floor. Disposition: mechanical. (8) Bespoke burn wording: oil and volatile reagents [15-equipment:132,148] say the victim takes fire damage each round until they spend an action to douse the flames; the conditions table has Burning X [13-combat:174] doing exactly this with scaling. Broken value: "1 ongoing fire damage" and "2 fire damage on hit" are not Burning X and do not scale; expected: Burning 1, scaling, one stacking rule. Disposition: mechanical. (9) Mount economy: heavy barding grants a mount +3 DR for 200 gp [15-equipment:178]; a warhorse (35 HP, +3 DR, attacked from the ground at -1) absorbs dozens of minimum-1 hits, so a 400 gp warhorse plus 200 gp barding is effectively unkillable by light weapons. Expected: mounts stay killable by focused fire or barding DR is capped. The +1/-1 mounted-versus-foot modifiers [15-equipment:207] are flat roll modifiers and consistent with the book's modifier law (cover -1, Defend +2); those survive. Disposition: design-decision; recommended default: cap barding DR or state mounts are valid targets. (10) Crossbow vs bow survives: the crossbow has Loading [15-equipment:70], requiring a Maneuver to reload between shots, with no damage advantage over the longbow, so it is not strictly better than a trained bow. (11) The crowbar Boon line survives: the chapter grants a Boon on Brawn checks to force doors [15-equipment:120], and the core resolution chapter defines a Boon as 4d6 keep highest 3 [06-core-resolution:45]; consistent, no damage interaction. (12) Command plus Charge: Command [13-combat:60] gives a mount an extra move as a maneuver, so a rider can Command-move the mount and then charge the same turn, charging without spending the mount's normal movement. Expected: charge requires movement from your own action. Disposition: design-decision; recommended default: require the charge movement to be yours. The one architectural fork everything turns on: the chapter treats charge as two independent rules and the mounted table introduces a flat damage bonus on top of a tier system whose law is "no flat +N damage riders". The fix is to unify charge into one rule with a tier-based rider and no flat addition, and to bound the chase contest so it terminates.

evidence.claim: The mounted charge table turns a Strong result into a flat +3 add-on, a damage expression the book elsewhere forbids; this is the chapter's architectural fault line.
The chase rule adds +1 for the higher-Speed side with ties narrated as complications, and the vehicle table gives Speed as "Draft animal" with no number to compare.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The side with the higher Speed rating gains +1

evidence.claim: Oil and volatile reagents inflict fire damage on hit plus a recurring burn ending only when the victim spends an action, bespoke phrasing duplicated across two items.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: 1 ongoing fire damage until they spend an action

evidence.claim: Several gear entries carry improvised-weapon damage values while the chapter never defines what an improvised weapon is.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Can be used as an improvised weapon (1/1/2 damage)

evidence.claim: Worked exploit math: a mounted greatsword Strong hit with a book tier bump reaches 13+ against Adept budget caps of 12; a 1-sp oil flask rivals Basic cards every round; a wagon wins a chase round versus a horse only about 28% of the time, enabling infinite stall.

payload.argument:
The chapter's voice mostly holds: the weapons intro, gear-table notes, mount lore, and chase flavor all match the book's punchy register, and the opening paragraph lands well. But it fails as a publishable unit on consistency grounds; several name and notation defects need fixing. Numbered audit:

1. [15:132, 15:148] Recurring fire damage is phrased as ad-hoc 'ongoing' damage with a bespoke douse action, bypassing the book's leveled condition vocabulary (Burning X per the conditions table and glossary, used by spells and items elsewhere). Expected: Burning 1 with the standard exit phrasing; the two cells also near-duplicate each other, so unify them. Disposition: mechanical.
2. [15:189 vs 09:461-469] The mounted tier-boost is named Charge Attack, while the polearm maneuver Brace triggers on the generic word 'charge' with no pointer to it; the chapter's own fiction also uses the bare word. Expected: one canonical name (keep Charge Attack) and a cross-reference from Brace's trigger. Disposition: substantive (naming plus a cross-file link).
3. [15:91 vs 13:330-334, 21:149] The tower shield 'provides half cover', borrowing a term the book defines as a terrain/position state imposing an attacker penalty; the effect on the wielder is never stated, and the armor chapter's fuller entry (with its plant-to-cover maneuver) is not mirrored here. Expected: state the shield's cover effect or reference the Cover rule, and align the summary with the armor chapter. Disposition: design-decision; recommended default: cross-reference the Cover table and spell out the effect.
4. [15:220-227] The vehicles table's Speed column contains non-numeric cells (an animal class, an animal class plus an unexplained minus-two, oars-or-sail) instead of speed values. Expected: numeric speeds or a defined reference to the draft animal's speed. Disposition: mechanical.
5. [15:231, 15:238-240] The chase contest compares 'Speed rating', but the vehicles table never provides a numeric rating for vehicles, and the speed bullet only says vehicles move at the animal's speed. Expected: a defined numeric speed (or rating) per vehicle so the contest is resolvable. Disposition: substantive.
6. [15:74-91] The Armor section is one dry line, a table, and a shield line with no voice beat, unlike the Weapons and gear openings. Expected: a short flavor sentence opening the section. Disposition: substantive.
7. [15:95-99] Encumbrance is four clipped declaratives with no register, the chapter's most stat-block-like passage. Expected: a brief voice line (book-style one-liner) before or after the numbers. Disposition: substantive.
8. [15:120-148] The gear table uses 'improvised weapon' for crowbar, hammer, and torch but 'improvised attack' for oil and volatile reagents, naming the same concept two ways on one table. Expected: a single term with per-item damage. Disposition: mechanical.
9. [15:210-212] The Cavalry Arrives callout restates the Charge Attack tier table in prose and softens the top row into vague praise instead of its actual value. Expected: trim the restatement and let the table carry the numbers. Disposition: mechanical.
10. [15:136, 15:149] Both deprivation ladders (rations, water) close with the same stock sentence. Expected: vary the second instance. Disposition: design-decision; recommended default: vary the wording.
11. [15:238-240] The chapter ends on the chase tip with no closing beat; sibling chapters close with guidance or a send-off. Expected: a short outro paragraph. Disposition: substantive.

evidence.claim: Two gear cells describe lingering fire damage with bespoke wording instead of the book's Burning X condition vocabulary, and the two cells nearly duplicate each other.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: 1 ongoing fire damage until they spend an action

evidence.claim: A polearm maneuver's tiers trigger on the generic word 'charge' with no pointer to the equipment chapter's named mounted charge rule.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: +2 DR against a charge; the attacker takes

evidence.claim: The tower shield entry borrows the positional cover term without defining what effect it grants the wielder.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Tower Shield (2 Protection, +3 DR, provides half cover)

evidence.claim: The vehicles table's speed column holds an animal class and an unexplained modifier instead of a speed value.
The encumbrance section delivers its rules with no voice beat, unlike every other section in the chapter.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Slot-based system. You have 10 + (Brawn x 5) slots.

payload.argument:
The chapter does not hold as a publishable unit on the final-quality lens. All four explicit cross-references resolve correctly (talents/abilities in ch09, combat in ch13, armor/shields in ch16, classes in ch05), and the text is clean of em-dashes, but the chapter fails on completeness, internal consistency, and one closing-balance check. Full audit:

1. [15:25-43] The weapon table carries no Damage column at all, yet ch08:197 explicitly promises the weapon damage curve lives in the Equipment chapter (daggers 1/2/3 up to greatswords 3/5/8, plus Brawn). The chapter's own Melee Damage note (15:52) says the weapon never changes the damage numbers, flatly contradicting ch08's curve. A player cannot learn a greatsword's damage from this chapter. Expected state: add a Damage column with Weak/Standard/Strong values on the ch08 curve, and reconcile the 15:52 note. Disposition: substantive (multi-file: ch15 table plus ch08 pointer).
2. [15:41-43] Shortbow, Longbow, and Crossbow have no range anywhere in the chapter; only Thrown gets a range (20/60 ft) in the Properties list (15:68). The Basic Archery card in ch09:257 sets 60/120 ft, so the value exists elsewhere but is absent here. Expected state: a Range column or per-weapon range entries for missile weapons. Disposition: mechanical.
3. [15:25-43] The weapon table's Cost column is empty for 16 of 17 rows; only Throwing Dagger (2 gp) is priced, while the gear and mount tables are fully priced and the intro (15:15) promises prices in gold. A player shopping for a sword outside their starting kit stalls. Expected state: fill all weapon costs, or drop the column and say the DA sets prices. Disposition: design-decision, recommended default is to fill costs for parity with the gear table.
4. [15:120, 15:125] Improvised weapon damage is a flat 1/1/2 with no attribute and no defining rule line anywhere; the term is only used inline in item notes. This sits off the weapon curve (1/2/3 to 3/5/8 + Brawn) and off the flat budget rows (2/4/6 etc.), and is strictly weaker than Basic Unarmed (1/1/2 + Brawn, ch09:287-295). Expected state: one rule line defining improvised weapons, with the row anchored to Basic Unarmed (1/1/2 + Brawn) or a budget row. Disposition: mechanical (budget row plus single insertion).
5. [15:132, 15:148] Oil and Volatile Reagents inflict recurring fire damage described with bespoke ongoing phrasing, ended by spending an action - but the book already standardizes exactly this shape as the Burning X condition (ch13:171: takes X damage per round, spend an action to end). Expected state: "applies Burning 1". Disposition: mechanical (vocabulary per standing convention).
6. [15:132, 15:148] The same two entries deal a single flat "2 fire damage on hit" with no tier row. Flat damage in the book is expressed as Weak/Standard/Strong rows (Novice 2/4/6); a lone 2 is an untiered value. Expected state: a tiered row (e.g., 2/4/6) or condition-only application. Disposition: mechanical (budget row).
7. [15:147] Torch used as an improvised weapon deals flat "1 fire damage", inconsistent with crowbar and hammer (1/1/2) and below every floor in the budget. Expected state: torch as improvised weapon deals 1/1/2 fire, matching the other improvised entries. Disposition: mechanical (budget value).
8. [15:218-227] The Vehicles table's Speed column contains propulsion labels ("Draft animal", "Oars or sail", "Sail + oars") rather than speeds, while the Mounts table's Speed column has real values (60 ft etc.); the vehicle rules (15:231) say a drawn vehicle moves at the animal's Speed. Expected state: rename the column to Propulsion, or enter actual speeds. Disposition: mechanical (column label/cells).
9. [15:160-240] Heading hierarchy inside Mounts & Vehicles is broken: real subsections are ### (Mounts, Mounted Combat, Vehicles) but Naming Your Mount (15:181), The Cavalry Arrives (15:210), and Chases (15:238) are ## headings inside callouts, so they outrank the section that contains them in the TOC; Chases - a real subsystem with a contest mechanic - is styled as a tip box. Expected state: demote the three callout titles to ###, and promote Chases to a genuine ## section. Disposition: mechanical (heading levels).
10. [15:95-97] Encumbrance is three lines with no worked example, so a player computing their carry load gets no check against the 10 + (Brawn x 5) formula (consistent with ch03:70). Expected state: one short example. Disposition: mechanical (insertion).

evidence.claim: The weapon table columns omit damage entirely and price only one of seventeen weapons, so the chapter delivers neither the damage curve nor usable prices.
The damage-budget chapter directs readers to the Equipment chapter for a weapon damage curve that this chapter never prints, and the 15:52 note denies weapons change damage.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: daggers 1/2/3 up to greatswords 3/5/8, plus Brawn

evidence.claim: Oil and volatile reagents use bespoke ongoing-fire phrasing for recurring damage instead of the leveled Burning condition the book standardizes.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: 1 ongoing fire damage until they spend an action

evidence.claim: The Burning X condition already exists with exactly the spend-an-action-to-end shape the equipment entries describe, making the bespoke phrasing unnecessary.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Burning X | Takes X damage per round

evidence.claim: The vehicles table labels a column Speed but fills it with propulsion types rather than measurements, unlike the mounts table.

payload.argument: The chapter renders correctly in the Typst build in most respects, but four presentation defects make it unfit to publish as-is. (1) [15-equipment.qmd:25-43] The weapons table's Cost column is blank on 17 of 18 rows, with only the Throwing Dagger row priced; the built PDF shows a near-empty column that wastes width and reads as unfinished, contradicting the chapter's own claim that prices are given in gp. Expected: every weapon priced or the column removed entirely. Disposition: design-decision; recommended default: populate all rows or drop the column. (2) [15-equipment.qmd:218-227] The vehicle table's Speed column mixes label-type values ('Draft animal', 'Oars or sail') with an unexplained parenthetical penalty, and in the render the '(-2)' marker wraps onto its own line under 'Draft animal'; the chase rule at line 239 compares 'Speed rating' but the table exposes no numeric rating to compare. Expected: numeric ratings or an explicit definition of the modifier, with a cell that does not strand '(-2)' on a second line. Disposition: design-decision with a mechanical wrap fix; recommended default: make Speed a defined rating and document the draft-animal penalty. (3) [15-equipment.qmd:95-97] The Encumbrance section is one sentence boxed between forced page breaks (lines 93 and 99), so the build gives it a nearly blank page (PDF p237) with the heading and two lines of text alone. Expected: share a page with adjacent content or fold the rules into the gear preamble. Disposition: mechanical (pagebreak placement); recommended default: remove one of the surrounding breaks or merge the section. (4) [15-equipment.qmd:27-43, 80-87 vs 16-armor-shields.qmd:31-38] Item-name bolding is inconsistent: gear, mount, and vehicle tables bold their first column, while this chapter's weapons and armor tables do not, and the sibling armor chapter bolds its armor names; the armor summary header 'Discipline Req' also diverges from ch16's 'Discipline'. Expected: uniform bold first column across all tables and an aligned armor header label. Disposition: mechanical. payload.rationale: Topic t-01 (audit ch15 Equipment as a publishable unit) fails by unanimous refute across all six lenses, 6/6, no supports, no rebuttals, no sealed rulings. The game-architect and researcher independently verified flat-rule violations against the book's locked conventions: the mounted Charge table's 'Strong + 3' cell [15-equipment:195] is a forbidden flat +N damage rider (legal bonus forms are budget rows, Basic-card 1/2/3 + attribute floors, or one-tier bumps), and it contradicts the land Charge card's one-tier-shift expression at 09-talents-abilities:447-455; the contrarian's stress test showed the fork is structural - charge is implemented as two independent rules, and combined with a tier-bump feature it produces 13+ damage on one hit against Adept budget caps of 12, an unbounded two-weapon stacking exploit, and an unresolvable 1d6 chase contest (no success threshold, no numeric Speed ratings, ties narrate instead of advance, so chases stall forever). Every other lens corroborates: the researcher verified 16 of 17 weapon cost cells are empty, the improvised 1/1/2 curve matches no weapon-ladder row, and the oil/reagents recurring-fire phrasing bypasses the existing Burning X condition; the editor-in-chief found the chapter contradicts ch08's damage-curve deferral, misses ranges, breaks heading/pagination flow, and lacks encumbrance examples; the author found name and notation collisions (improvised weapon vs improvised attack, Charge Attack vs bare 'charge', stale full-rest vocabulary) and voice gaps; the layout-expert confirmed the empty Cost column, the non-numeric vehicle Speed cells with a wrapping '(-2)', and a pagebreak-isolated Encumbrance section in the built PDF. Where findings conflict, the layout expert's verified build check resolves it: callout titles at ## inside callout divs do not pollute the TOC (it lists only the five top-level sections), so the editor-in-chief's heading-demotion item is dropped and the real layout defect is the pagebreak placement. The chapter is close to publishable (em-dash law holds, all four cross-references resolve, armor values match ch16, crowbar Boon and draft-horse Bane match ch06, half cover matches the ch13 cover table, kit weapons and discipline combos are sound), but the mechanics contradictions against locked conventions and the unresolvable chase rule mean it cannot ship as a unit; the disposition plan above tiers every defect, so a re-audit after the mechanical micro-PRs, the four dispatched passes, and Bruce's rulings on the four design defaults is sufficient to reach a supportable state.
payload.recommendation: VERDICT: t-01 REJECTED as a publishable unit (6/6 refutes, unanimous, no rebuttals, no sealed rulings). ch15 (15-equipment.qmd) must not ship as-is; re-audit after the disposition plan below lands. DISPOSITION PLAN. (a) MECHANICAL (12 safe single-file micro-PRs): M1 [15-equipment:195] Charge table top cell 'Strong | Strong + 3' -> tier cap with no flat adder (expected 'Strong | Strong'), unifying the mounted table with the land Charge card's one-tier-shift expression at 09-talents-abilities:447-455; this also closes the contrarian's stacking exploit (land Charge +1 tier + flat 3 + Battle Cry tier = 13+ off one hit vs the Adept 12 cap) and implies a 'one charge benefit per attack' limit so the off-hand two-weapon attack cannot also claim the charge benefit. M2 [15-equipment:132,148] Oil (flask) and Volatile Reagents: replace bespoke '1 ongoing fire damage until they spend an action' with 'applies Burning 1' per the ch13 conditions table (13-combat:174), unifying the two near-duplicate cells. M3 [15-equipment:147] Torch '1 fire damage on hit' -> '1/1/2 fire' to match the crowbar/hammer improvised parentheticals. M4 [15-equipment:120,125] Improvised weapon parentheticals '(1/1/2 damage)' -> '(1/1/2 + Brawn)', anchoring improvised weapons to the Basic Unarmed card (09-talents-abilities:287-295) and stating the improvised-weapon rule once in the chapter. M5 [15-equipment:52] Melee Damage note 'Missile and thrown attacks add Agility' -> flat, no attribute added, per 08-disciplines:195 and the flat 1/2/3 Basic Archery/Thrown cards (09-talents-abilities:257-277). M6 [15-equipment:199] Controlling a Mount: stop redefining Command as mount direction; movement/steering is free and the Command maneuver (13-combat:60) grants the mount an extra move; the Survival/Nature control check stays as a separate DA-called rule, reconciled in one pass with ch13. M7 [15-equipment:116] Bedroll 'Required for a full rest in the wild... recover half HP (rounded down) from rest' -> 'long rest' vocabulary (ch19:95-103) with recovery phrased as half the long-rest recovery, rounded down. M8 [15-equipment:118] Caltrops 'halve its speed until the end of its next turn' -> Slowed X condition with a stated feet reduction per 13-combat:187. M9 [15-equipment:25-43] Weapon table: add Range values for Shortbow/Longbow (60/120 ft, per 09-talents-abilities:259) and keep the Thrown 20/60 ft convention for thrown weapons. M10 [15-equipment:97,99] Encumbrance: remove one of the surrounding forced pagebreaks so the section stops rendering alone on a page, and add one short worked example of the 10 + (Brawn x 5) slots formula. M11 [15-equipment:27-43,80-87] Bold the first column of the weapons and armor tables to match ch16's bolded armor names (16-armor-shields:31-38) and rename the armor header 'Discipline Req' to 'Discipline'. M12 [15-equipment:210-212] Trim the Cavalry Arrives callout so it no longer restates the Charge Attack tier table in prose (let the table carry the numbers); note the callout titles at ## inside callout divs are book convention per the layout-expert's verified build (TOC lists only the five top-level sections), so no heading-level change is required. (b) SUBSTANTIVE (4 dispatched implementation passes): S1 [15-equipment:239] Vehicle chase: rewrite as a bounded, resolvable one-roll opposed contest - define what counts as a success, compare numeric Speed ratings, add a tie-break and a termination bound so chases end in a fixed number of rounds instead of stalling forever (ties currently produce narration, not progress; a draft-animal wagon wins a round vs a riding horse only ~28% of the time). S2 [15-equipment:174,220-227,231,239] Vehicle Speed: put numeric speeds in the Speed column (or a defined pointer to the draft animal's rating) and document the 'Draft animal (-2)' carriage/chariot penalty, so the chase rule's 'higher Speed rating' comparison has values to compare; wagon-vs-horse (40 vs 60 ft) is a 10-point gap the single +1 rule cannot represent. S3 [15-equipment:132,148] Oil economy: cap the 1-sp flask exploit - add a per-encounter limit or capped stacking so trivial coin cannot out-damage every Basic attack card each round; land together with M2. S4 [15-equipment:74-91,95-99,238-240] Voice pass: add an opening flavor beat to Armor, a one-line register beat to Encumbrance, and a short chapter outro after the Chases tip; vary the stock sentence closing the rations and waterskin deprivation ladders [15:136,149]; keep Charge Attack as the canonical name and add a cross-reference from Brace's 'charge' trigger (09-talents-abilities:461-469). (c) DESIGN-DECISION (4 need Bruce; implement each recommended default, logged veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md): D1 [15-equipment:25-43,52 vs 08-disciplines:197] Weapon damage curve: the budget chapter promises the per-weapon curve (dagger 1/2/3 to greatsword 3/5/8) lives in Equipment, but the weapon table has no Damage column and the Melee Damage note says the weapon never changes damage; default: keep the cards-are-damage design (09-talents-abilities:239: weapon disciplines gate stronger cards, not higher damage) and correct ch08's deferral instead of adding a column. D2 [15-equipment:120,125,147] Improvised weapon curve: the 1/1/2 parentheticals match no row on the 1/2/3-to-3/5/8 ladder; default: anchor improvised weapons to Basic Unarmed at 1/1/2 + Brawn (mechanical M4) and define the rule once here. D3 [15-equipment:25-43] Weapon Cost column: 16 of 17 rows are blank while the chapter promises gp pricing; default: populate all weapon costs for parity with the fully priced gear and mount tables. D4 [15-equipment:201] Moving-mount ranged penalty: the -2 flat (reduced to odd -1 at Adept) sits outside the book's even-step ladder and Boon/Bane convention (the mounted-vs-foot +1/-1 at [15-equipment:207] are consistent with the modifier law and survive); default: Bane on ranged attacks from a moving mount at Novice, Bane dropped at Adept+ Survival/Nature, ignored at Master. Also design-flagged, for Bruce to fold into D1/D4's session: [15-equipment:178] heavy barding (+3 DR, 200 gp) makes a 600 gp warhorse effectively unkillable by light weapons - default: cap barding DR or state mounts remain valid targets of focused fire.
